thread:
alex.t: Heads-up — noticed a latency blip after the kernel selector change last night. Canary CPU p95 went from 220ms -> 250ms. I ran a quick nsys trace and the act of tracing seems to bump tails. Need a plan for safe profiling in prod (sampling vs full).

maria.k: Do we have the raw numbers for tracing overhead? Was KV cache cold at the time? Could be masking the regression.

chen: When I instrumented with nvprof a while back I saw ~18–22% overhead on short lived requests. nsys tends to be better but full qdrep captures can still inflate tails if we do them too often. Sampling mode is much cheaper.

alex.t: Quick summary of what I ran locally:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --output=trace.qdrep --sample=cpu --capture-range=nvtx:kernel_start:kernel_end --duration=30
```
That produced a 30s capture and I saw p99 shift +8% during that window on the canary.

infra-bot: deploy bot: canary rollouts paused for latency regression investigation (:eyes:).

sam: For prod guardrails I'd propose:
- Default to lightweight sampling (1 in 50 requests) for continuous profiling.
- Only enable full qdrep captures for short windows (<=30s) and <5% of traffic.
- Autoscrub PII and keys before upload.
- Drop full traces if KV cache hit ratio < threshold to avoid cold-start noise.

maria.k: +1. Also we should correlate with batch size and KV cache hits. If a request triggers a cache miss, you get more kernel launches (smaller kernels) and tracing overhead becomes disproportionate.

chen: Measured numbers from my bench: sampling mode (1/20) added ~1.2% median and ~1.6% p95. Full 30s qdrep on same host -> median +6%, p95 +12%. Those are with 8xA100 config, medium batch (bs=8). Warm cache vs cold cache differences: cold adds ~10–15% extra kernel invocations.

alex.t: Good — that helps. So we should avoid full captures during cache warmup windows. How do we detect that?

sam: We can use a short pre-sample to estimate KV stats: record KV hits/misses for 5s and if miss_rate>5% skip full capture. Also rate-limit by request path and model.

maria.k: Proposed safe flow:
1) Continuous sampling @1/50 global.
2) On anomaly (latency spike or error rate bump), trigger targeted sampling 1/10 for 60s.
3) If anomaly persists and kv_miss_rate <5% and we have infra approval, run a 20–30s full nsys capture on a shard (cap 3 captures/hour).
4) Auto-scrub & encrypt then upload to internal S3.

chen: For the upload and scrub step, use a lightweight binary scrubber that strips request text and replaces with token counts. We should also strip env vars and keys from metadata in qdrep before storage.

alex.t: Can someone post the exact safe nsys command we'll standardize? And the S3 upload snippet + scrub step.

maria.k: Drafting one now:
```
# safe nsys invocation (full capture, short window)
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --output=/tmp/prod_capture.qdrep \
  --capture-range=nvtx:kernel_start:kernel_end \
  --force-overwrite --sample=cpu --duration=20

# scrubper (pseudo)
./qdrep-scrubber --input /tmp/prod_capture.qdrep --strip-text --strip-env --out /tmp/prod_capture.scrub.qdrep

# upload with tags and encryption
aws s3 cp /tmp/prod_capture.scrub.qdrep s3://redwood-profiler-prod/ --sse aws:kms --tagging "env=prod,team=rt"
```

oliver: I'll add a feature flag + rate-limit enforcement to infra so nobody accidentally enables full traces by default. Also adding an audit log for each capture.

sam: We should add metrics to the console: tracing_overhead_{median,p95,p99} and capture_count by model + kv_miss_rate at start_of_capture. That will let SREs decide if captures are safe.

alex.t: OK — next steps: maria to draft runbook + command snippets, oliver to add feature flag + audit logs, chen to run controlled A/B bench comparing sampling ratios (1/20,1/50,1/100) and report overhead numbers, sam to add dashboard panels and alerts. I'll coordinate a short on-call drill for aborting captures if a regression is detected.

maria.k: Will do. Posting runbook PR within today.

chen: I'll start bench runs now and dump results in #perf-reports. Expect CSV with per-kernel timelines.

infra-bot: scheduled job: add capture rate-limit feature created by oliver.

alex.t: Thanks everyone. If you find anything blocking the runbook or flags, ping me. :thumbsup:
